classification.difficultyReason: Translate the claim about distinct quadratic roots into strict positivity of the discriminant, then use the trigonometric identity to obtain a positive lower bound for every angle.

content.prompt: Show that $x^2-x\sin\alpha-\cos^2\alpha=0$ will always have two distinct solutions of $x$.

answer.short:
$\Delta=\sin^2\alpha+4\cos^2\alpha=1+3\cos^2\alpha\geq1>0$.

A positive discriminant gives two distinct real solutions.
answer.worked:
For the quadratic in $x$, the discriminant is
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-\sin\alpha)^2-4(1)(-\cos^2\alpha)\\\Delta&=\sin^2\alpha+4\cos^2\alpha\\\Delta&=1+3\cos^2\alpha\geq1>0.\end{align*}$$
Hence the equation has two distinct real solutions for every real $\alpha$.
